newsitem.title: ITALY: Cuba not in Stet-At&T Latinamerican deal -Stet.
newsitem.headline: Cuba not in Stet-At&T Latinamerican deal -Stet.

text.p: Cuba is not involved in the Latin America deal agreed by Italian telecoms holding Stet and AT&T Corp, Stet's managing director said on Wednesday.
"Cuba was kept out of the agreement," Tomaso Tommasi di Vignano told a news conference on the global telecoms alliance between the two groups.
In Latin America, Stet/Telecom Italia and AT&T will form a 50-50 joint venture that will deliver a portfolio of global services.
"There are great opportunities even in the next few months," Tommasi said, referring to the two partners' joint bid to enter Brazil's mobile phone market.
Stet already has a considerable presence in Latin America, Tommasi noted, where it has "two billion dollars of assets and has installed four million fixed phone lines."
He said it was a region of strong telecoms growth. "In four years we expect growth in the telephony market of 70 percent."
He added that the global accord with At&T, for both Latin America as well as Europe, would be fully defined by the end of this year.
